questions.question: The ulna is the medial bone of which part of the body?
questions.explanation: The ulna is described as the medial bone of the forearm.

questions.question: The ulna is homologous to which bone of the lower limb?
questions.explanation: The ulna is homologous to the lateral bone of the leg, which is the fibula.

questions.question: The ulna consists of three parts. Which of the following is one of them?
questions.explanation: The ulna consists of the upper end, lower end, and shaft.

questions.question: What is the shape of the upper end of the ulna?
questions.explanation: The upper end is expanded and hook-like with the concavity facing forwards.

questions.question: Which notch lies between the olecranon and coronoid processes?
questions.explanation: The concavity of the upper end, known as the trochlear notch, lies between the olecranon and coronoid processes.

questions.question: How does the thickness of the ulnar shaft change from above downwards?
questions.explanation: The thickness of the shaft diminishes progressively from above downwards throughout its length.

questions.question: The styloid process is located at which part of the ulna?
questions.explanation: The lower end of the ulna is slightly expanded and has a head and styloid process.

questions.question: Where is the styloid process situated in relation to the ulnar head?
questions.explanation: The styloid process is located posteromedial to the head of the ulna.

questions.question: During side determination, which border of the ulna is directed laterally?
questions.explanation: The sharp crest-like interosseous border of the shaft is directed laterally during side determination.

questions.question: Which structure inserts on the rough posterior two-thirds of the olecranon's upper surface?
questions.explanation: The rough posterior two-thirds of the olecranon's upper surface provides insertion to the triceps brachii.

questions.question: What is found on the posterior surface of the olecranon?
questions.explanation: A subcutaneous olecranon bursa lies between the posterior surface of the olecranon and the skin.

questions.question: Which process of the ulna is described as a bracket-like projection?
questions.explanation: The coronoid process is a bracket-like projection from the front of the upper end of the ulna.

questions.question: The brachialis muscle is inserted into which structure?
questions.explanation: The brachialis muscle is inserted into the whole of the anterior surface of the coronoid process.

questions.question: What is the small tubercle at the upper end of the medial margin of the coronoid process called?
questions.explanation: The medial margin of the anterior surface has a tubercle at its upper end called the sublime tubercle.

questions.question: Which muscle originates from the medial surface of the coronoid process?
questions.explanation: The medial surface of the coronoid process gives origin to the flexor digitorum profundus.

questions.question: The radial notch is located on which surface of the coronoid process?
questions.explanation: The lateral surface of the coronoid process possesses a radial notch for articulation with the head of the radius.

questions.question: Which ligament attaches to the anterior and posterior margins of the radial notch?
questions.explanation: The annular ligament is attached to the anterior and posterior margins of the radial notch.

questions.question: What is the depression below the radial notch called?
questions.explanation: The lower part of the lateral surface below the radial notch has a depressed area called the supinator fossa.

questions.question: Which muscle originates from the supinator crest?
questions.explanation: The supinator crest and adjoining part of the supinator fossa give origin to the supinator muscle.

questions.question: What is the shape of the trochlear notch?
questions.explanation: The trochlear notch is C-shaped (semilunar) and articulates with the trochlea of the humerus.

questions.question: The trochlear notch articulates with which structure?
questions.explanation: The trochlear notch articulates with the trochlea of the humerus.

questions.question: A non-articular strip is found at the junction of which two parts?
questions.explanation: The trochlear notch has a non-articular strip at the junction of its olecranon and coronoid parts.

questions.question: Which border is the sharpest and continuous with the supinator crest?
questions.explanation: The lateral (interosseous) border is the sharpest and is continuous above with the supinator crest.

questions.question: To which border of the ulna is the interosseous membrane attached?
questions.explanation: The interosseous membrane is attached to the lateral border except for its upper part.

questions.question: The upper three-fourths of the anterior border gives origin to which muscle?
questions.explanation: The upper three-fourths of the anterior border gives origin to the flexor digitorum profundus.

questions.question: Which border is subcutaneous throughout its entire length?
questions.explanation: The posterior border is subcutaneous throughout, hence it can be palpated along its entire length.

questions.question: Which of the following muscles attaches to the posterior border by a common aponeurosis?
questions.explanation: The posterior border provides attachment to the flexor digitorum profundus, flexor carpi ulnaris, and extensor carpi ulnaris by a common aponeurosis.

questions.question: Where does the posterior border of the ulna start?
questions.explanation: The posterior border starts from the apex of the triangular subcutaneous area on the back of the olecranon process.

questions.question: How many borders and surfaces does the ulnar shaft have?
questions.explanation: The shaft of the ulna has three borders (lateral, anterior, posterior) and three surfaces.

questions.question: Which structure forms the superior part of the trochlear notch?
questions.explanation: The anterior surface of the olecranon process forms the upper part of the trochlear notch.
